item.description:
### Block a whole category, except the one site you need
Block lists used to be all-or-nothing: adding the Social category blocked all 30 of its sites, and there was no way to keep one of them. The Exceptions tab now carves sites out of what the list blocks — block Social, except linkedin.com — and it works down to a single subdomain, so you can block reddit.com while old.reddit.com still opens. A spent daily limit still wins over an exception.
Exceptions used to mean something else: a list could be a whitelist that blocked everything on the Mac except a few chosen apps. That mode is gone, and any list you had set up that way now shows its sites under Exceptions with nothing blocked, ready for you to say what it should block.
### Website time limits actually count
A limit on youtube.com never counted the time you spent there. Browsers send you to www.youtube.com, and the minutes were filed under that name instead — so the budget never filled, the countdown never appeared, and the site was never blocked. Time now counts against the site you named, subdomains included: a limit on youtube.com covers m.youtube.com too.
A new limit also starts from zero. It used to count the whole day, so a 10-minute limit set up after an hour on a site blocked it immediately.
### A countdown you can read, and ignore
The remaining-time pill sat over the browser's address bar in small type. It now sits in the bottom-right corner at a readable size, faded back so it doesn't compete with the page — move the pointer over it and it comes up to full.
